newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
EX-PRIME MINISTER RAO SEEKS ANTICIPATORY BAIL

Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao moved the Delhi High Court seeking anticipatory bail fearing arrest in the Lakhubhai Pathak cheating case. The former prime minister is appearing before Additional District and Sessions Judge on September 30 in the case. Following Rao's application, the Delhi High Court issued notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation to show cause as to why Rao's plea for anticipatory bail should not be admitted.
The Pioneer
BULLETS IMPLANTED IN POLICEMEN'S BODIES AS PROOF OF VIOLENCE

Muzaffarnagar district administration has been held responsible for police attrocities committed on Uttarakhand agitators in October 1994. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has established that the district administration manufactured evidence to cover up police atrocities on the agitators. In 1994 thousands of agitators demanding separate statehood for the Uttarakhand region in Uttar Pradesh were assulted by the police and women raped. CBI found unfired bullets were surgically implanted under the skin of five constables as evidence that Uttarakhand demonstrators had used firearms against the police.
Financial Express
FDI IN UNLISTED COMPANIES RAISED TO 51 PCT

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised the foreign direct investment (FDI) limit in unlisted companies to 51 percent on a repatriable basis. This is aimed at attracting greater FDI from non-resident Indians (NRIs). RBI's existing scheme allowing NRIs to invest up to 40 percent thus stands abolished. The central bank has put norms for NRI participation in venture capital companies at par with foreign investors.
BPL TO RAISE $200 MLN FROM AMERICAN MARKET

BPL group's BPL Cellular Holding Ltd is raising $200 million through an issue of American Depository Receipts. The issue, to be listed on NASDAQ, will have a greenshoe option of 15 percent. The issue will be offered via an SEC registered initial public offering. The company is awaiting the final approval of the government.
BIDS FOR OIL EXPLORATION IN SEVEN BLOCKS CLEARED

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) has accorded clearance to several bids for oil and gas exploration and some under offers for development of small-sized fields. CCEA has cleared seven blocks as per the recommendation of the Empowered Committee of Secretaries. A total of 33 bids for 18 blocks were received for the 34 blocks offered. Of these, U.S. companies Occidental International Exploration and Production Company were awarded two onshore blocks AA ON 4 and AA ON 6 in the Assam Arakan region. The Assam Company Limited and US based Medallion Company togather bagged AA ON 7 while Reliance-Enron combine got BB-OS/8.
CENTRAL BANK TO EASE FOREIGN CURRENCY DEPOSIT NORMS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will soon allow select non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) to raise deposits in foreign currency. These deposits would be similar to the foreign currency non-resident deposits allowed to banks. Sources said the NBFCs would bear the exchange risk on these deposits.
The Economic Times
BANK WITH 10.5 BLN RUPEE CAPITAL PLANNED

A group of Gulf-based non-resident Indians (NRIs) has proposed to set up a private bank with a capital base of 10.5 billion rupees. The new bank, to be called Trade and Commerce Bank, would be registered in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. Sources said the NRIs would be putting up 38 percent, or four billion rupees, of the total equity and the investment would be made on a repatriable basis.
BHARAT PETROLEUM FIGHTS SHY OF MAIDEN ISSUE

Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL) plans to defer its 4.5 billion rupee public issue because of poor market conditions. The issue was to hit the market this October. BPCL had filed a price band of 270 to 320 rupees with the bourse regulator. The public sector major, however, is yet to formally put its applications with the Registrar of Companies.
Business Standard
FOREIGN BANKS RUSH FOR GILTS

Foreign banks have turned speculators in the securities market as secondary debt market trading touched 2.18 billion rupee mark on the National Stock Exchange. With most of the nationalised banks turning sellers, the foreign banks have stepped into the debt market to make a quick buck. This has pepped up activity in the debt market. Treasury heads with foreign banks said they were not lending their money to the corporate sector but were, instead, deploying the funds in the short term securities.
INDIA FIGHTS BID TO TRAMMEL RIGHT TO REGULATE INVESTMENT

India plans to oppose the multilateral agreement on investment (MAI) being pushed by the OECD countries. It further plans to insist on retaining government rights to regulate foreign direct investment inflows. India would place its views at the coming MAI meet at Delhi to thrash out a common viewpoint for developing countries on emerging trade issues. Nineteen developing countries have been invited for the meet, of which 10 have confirmed participation, including Pakistan and Bangladesh.
TATA'S SMALL CAR TO MATERIALISE IN 1998

Tata Engineering & Locomotive Co Ltd (TELCO) plans to launch its small passenger car in 1998. Company sources said the car would be a utility vehicle in the 800-1000cc range. While pricing has not been worked out, it would be competing with the Maruti 800 and the Zen, the sources added. The company plans to set up a 150,000 per year capacity car unit. The plant will be part of the comprehensive facility being set up by TELCO. This will have flexible lines capable of manufacturing the small car, the Sumo and other models.
The Observer
ITC CLASSIC TO SEEK NOD FOR GDR

ITC Classic Finance Ltd, a subsidiary of ITC Ltd, is seeking shareholders' approval for raising $45 million loan from the International Finance Corporation (IFC). The loan from IFC is for on-lending to export oriented eligible companies for equipment finance, foreign capital expenditure and infrastructural project finance. The company is also planning to raise $25 million through an issue of Global Depository Receipts at a later date.
Business Line
63 FDI PROPOSALS CLEARED

The Industry Ministry has cleared 63 foreign direct investment proposals amounting to 54.1 billion rupees. The proposals have total export projection up to 19 billion rupees over five to seven years. The proposals relate to software, engineering, electronics, power cotton and synthetic yarn, floriculture, financial services, medical services and pharmaceuticals. The major companies whose proposals with 100 percent foreign equity have been approved include G.M. Iocomotive Group ($5 millions) for support services to the Railways, Micon AS Denmark (100 million rupees) for the construction of a wind turbine power plant. E.M. Warburg, Pincus and Co. Inc. New York, has agreed to pump in 371 million rupees to market and distribute telecom hardware for cellular and paging services. Viba Siat S.R.I. of Italy with an investment of seven million rupees plans to carry on activities in the field of machinery for manufacture of synthetic fibre.
